title: Steering a vision-language model with a text-derived safety vector

original_idea.body: Extract a harm/refusal direction from text-only contrastive pairs in a small open VLM, then test whether it steers/probes when harmful content arrives via an image.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: cross-modal safety-vector reuse defends a growing multimodal jailbreak surface.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Small open VLM + text-derived direction; guided but VLM internals add friction.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Under-defended multimodal surface, open models, independent-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: Small VLM inference on one GPU, no training.

novelty.reasoning: VLM refusal steering exists; text-derived cross-modal transfer may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Text-to-image cross-modal safety transfer may be open.
